Make a PHW-styled flextable from a data frame

Source: R/flextable.R
phw_flextable.Rd

One call that builds a flextable, formats numbers with thousands separators, applies phw_flextable_theme() and adds the PHW caption and source line. The caption ("Table 1 ...") goes above and the bold source goes below, right-aligned.

Usage

phw_flextable(
  data,
  caption = NULL,
  number = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  date = NULL,
  style = "booktabs",
  digits = 1,
  col_labels = NULL,
  autofit = TRUE,
  number_prefix = "Table",
  caption_args = list(),
  flextable_args = list(),
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, or a summary table from phw_summary_table(), phw_crosstab(), phw_rate_table() or phw_risk_table(). Summary tables get bold variable headings, indented levels, a header spanning the group columns and a note on the statistics shown.

caption

Table title, e.g. "Counts by health board, 2020-2024".

number

Optional table number. Gives "Table 1 ...".

source, date

Passed to phw_caption() and shown under the table.

style

Passed to phw_flextable_theme().

digits

Decimal places for non-integer numbers.

col_labels

Optional named list of display names, as in flextable::set_header_labels().

autofit

Fit column widths to their content?

number_prefix

Word before the number.

caption_args

List of other phw_caption() arguments, e.g. list(note = "Provisional").

flextable_args

List of arguments for flextable::flextable(), e.g. list(col_keys = c("area", "rate")).

...

Passed to phw_flextable_theme().

Value

A flextable.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("flextable", quietly = TRUE)) {
  phw_flextable(head(mtcars[, 1:4]), caption = "Example", source = "mtcars")
}
